title: Tenant-scoped degradations and region-affinity circuit breakers for Dedicated/Private control planes
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Background: Dedicated and Private customers require deterministic behavior during upgrades, regional outages, and noisy-tenant incidents. Our current model-level fallbacks and topology-level failovers are coarse-grained: they either route an entire tenant to a different region or apply global throttles. This leads to expensive cross-region traffic, unnecessary full-tenant evacuation, and poor QoE for unaffected parts of a tenant's workload.

Problem statement: We need a fine-grained safety mechanism that can: (1) isolate problematic tenants or traffic classes without evicting all their workloads; (2) prefer region-affinity and minimize cross-region state transfers during failover; (3) apply graduated circuit-breaking and load-shedding policies tied to tenant SLOs and workload classes; (4) integrate with rolling upgrades for control-plane and runtime changes to enable safe, fast rollbacks.

Goals:
- Implement tenant-scoped degradations (graceful feature/quality reduction per-tenant) that preserve critical requests while shedding non-essential work.
- Introduce region-affinity circuit breakers so failover only occurs when data-plane compatibility is lost or capacity is exhausted in-region.
- Expose tenant policies in the control plane and Redwood Console with sane defaults and an opt-in deterministic "upgrade-safety" mode for Private deployments.
- Ensure observability and automated runbooks trigger precise mitigation actions with human-in-loop safety gates.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Tenant Isolation Levels: define three, tiered isolation modes: SOFT_DEGRADE (drop background/low-priority requests and reduce batch sizes), HARD_ISOLATE (route heavy traffic to a dedicated degraded pool within-region), EVICT_REGION (cross-region failover when in-region state is unrecoverable). Policies are evaluated per-tenant, per-route, and per-priority.

2) Region-Affinity Circuit Breaker: a control-plane component that computes an "affinity score" per tenant-region based on KV-cache warmness, recent error-rate deltas, infra-saturation signals, and SLO headroom. Breaker trips only when both capacity and affinity fall below configured thresholds for a sustained window. Breakers prefer degraded in-region behavior before cross-region routing.

3) Rolling-upgrade safety gates: augment the upgrade orchestrator with per-tenant canary gates. Before advancing a control-plane or runtime upgrade to a new cohort, run a tenant-impact simulation and small tenant canary (1–2 tenants). If tail latency or token-error regressions exceed thresholds, automatically pause and mark affected tenants as SOFT_DEGRADE until rollback completes.

4) Load-shedding policy engine: declarative policies (JSON schema surfaced in Console) that map traffic class -> tiered shedding actions. Default mapping: low-priority background jobs -> immediate drop under overload; embeddings bulk -> queue + reject-after-10s; interactive chat -> reduced max_tokens and increased batching.

Telemetry & SLOs:
- New SLOs to track per-tenant: p99 latency (generation), error-rate (4xx/5xx), and successful-embeddings per-second. Define degraded-SLOs for SOFT_DEGRADE and HARD_ISOLATE modes to reflect allowed lower QoE during incidents.
- Dashboards: per-tenant SLO trends, affinity score heatmaps, breaker event timeline, upgrade-cohort metrics.

Runbooks & safety:
- Automated runbooks that surface the exact set of tenants affected, the policy applied, and suggested remediation steps. Human confirmation required for EVICT_REGION actions in Private deployments.
- Oncall alerts mapped to a small set of high-confidence signals to avoid noise (sustained p99 regression + affinity drop + infra saturation).

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (design + internal spec): finalize policy schema, affinity scoring algorithm, and upgrade gating signals. (owner: Diego)
- Phase 1 (PoC): implement breaker controller and tenant isolation simulator in staging. Add synthetic tenants and chaos tests. (2 weeks)
- Phase 2 (canary): enable on a subset of Dedicated customers and 1 Private sandbox customer with opt-in flag. Monitor for 2 weeks.
- Phase 3 (ramp): expand to 25% of tenants with automated rollouts and Console controls.
- Phase 4 (GA): enable defaults for new Dedicated clusters and provide migration docs for Private.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for policy evaluation and scoring.
- Integration tests simulating KV-cold start, per-tenant burst, and region-partition with traffic replay.
- Chaos experiments: node failure, full-region network blackhole, degraded storage latencies.
- Preflight dry-run: run the upgrade-orchestrator in "simulate" mode against production traces to predict tenant impact before actual upgrades.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: misconfiguration isolates healthy tenants. Mitigation: conservative defaults, staged rollouts, dry-run simulation, manual approval for EVICT_REGION.
- Risk: increased control-plane complexity and operator burden. Mitigation: rich Console UX, sensible presets, and operator CLI helpers.
- Risk: observability gaps for legacy private installs. Mitigation: require minimal telemetry shims as part of Private install checklist.

Success metrics:
- Reduce cross-region evictions during incidents by >= 70% for dedicated clusters in the first 90 days post-GA.
- Decrease mean time to mitigation for noisy-tenant incidents from current baseline by 50%.
- No more than 1 P0 customer-facing incident attributable to automation bugs during rollout.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

acceptance_criteria: Policy schema defined and validated against JSON schema with documented defaults
Breaker controller PoC able to evaluate affinity score and emit decisions in staging
Upgrade-orchestrator can run tenant-impact simulation with >95% fidelity against replayed traces
Automated runbook generation lists affected tenants and recommended mitigation, with human approval for EVICT_REGION
Canary rollout completed for 3 Dedicated customers with no customer-facing regressions
comments: 2025-02-11: Kickoff meeting with Eng/PM/SRE. Agreed on three isolation modes and upfront need for per-tenant SLOs. Action: Diego to draft affinity scoring proposal.
2025-02-25: Design review — PM (Ava Chen) requested clearer upgrade-gating signals; Security (Liam O'Connor) flagged telemetry requirements for Private installs.
2025-03-05: PoC completed in staging: breaker controller correctly preferred SOFT_DEGRADE for synthetic noisy tenants and avoided cross-region routing in 93% of trials.
2025-03-12: Integrations meeting: runtime-1.20 needs a small API extension to report KV-warmness; added dependency 'runtime-1.20' to the release plan.
2025-03-18: Canary kickoff with two Dedicated customers (opt-in). Observability hooks deployed; first 48h show expected p99 uplift in degraded tenants and no cross-region evictions.
